request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 2.)

concerns: Best PR-AUC is run 1 (LightGBM, 0.731), but its edge over the best logistic (run 5, 0.6934) is 0.0376, which is smaller than one fold SD (about 0.065). Under the simplicity rule the simpler model is preferred.
Fold SDs of 0.064-0.077 are larger than nearly all gaps between configs, so the ranking is mostly noise. Run 1, run 4 and run 7 are statistically indistinguishable.
Precision@50 is 0.74-0.79 across all configs, so the audit queue of about 100 is similarly good under any model. Prec@50 does not measure the queue size of 100 directly.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 for every model, including logistic regression, is high. Together with the undocumented origin of the PotentialFraud label, the label may be derived from or correlated with the features, for example through claim volume, size or agent proxies. Treat the results as suspicion ranking, not validated fraud detection.

Run 5 uses the all+agent feature set, which includes size features and agent features. Size features can proxy for provider volume instead of fraud behavior, and the no_size results are close, so the signal may be mostly volume-driven. The feature gap is small: run 3 (no_size+agent, logistic) scores 0.676 and run 6 scores 0.692.
Only 7 configs were tried and the search was not systematic. The 9.35% positive rate gives about 500 positives, so fold estimates are noisy.
The claims window is under 13 months, so temporal leakage or label timing are possible and cannot be ruled out from this data. The CV scheme was not described.
